description: The plot illustrates the relationship between population frequency and accuracy, comparing initial and final accuracy values. The x-axis represents population frequency, scaled by a factor of 10^4, with a linear scale ranging from 1 to 17, and tick labels at intervals of 2. The y-axis represents accuracy, with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, and tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The green line, representing initial accuracy, starts at approximately 0.4 at an x-value of 1, fluctuates between 0.4 and 0.6 until an x-value of 9, then increases to around 0.8 at an x-value of 11, before stabilizing between 0.8 and 0.85 for x-values between 13 and 17. The blue line, representing final accuracy, begins at around 0.65 at an x-value of 1, generally increases with some fluctuations, reaching a peak of approximately 1.1 at an x-value of 17, with notable values including 0.9 at an x-value of 3, 1.1 at an x-value of 7, and 1.0 at an x-value of 11. Both lines are solid, with the green line marked by plus signs and the blue line marked by diamonds, and both have error bars indicating the range of values.
